title: Philippians Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Philippians chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Philippians Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Philippians Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Philippians 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: If there be therefore any consolation in Christ
Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory
Let this mind be in you
Being found in fashion as a man
questions.correctAnswer: If there be therefore any consolation in Christ
questions.explanation: This phrase appears in the very first verse of the chapter, Philippians 2:1.

questions.question: What does Paul ask the Philippians to fulfill in Philippians 2:2?
questions.explanation: Paul specifically states in Philippians 2:2, 'Fulfil ye my joy.'

questions.question: According to Philippians 2:3, what should be the attitude of believers in their interactions?
options: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory
Look not every man on his own things
Let this mind be in you
questions.correctAnswer: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:3 instructs believers to avoid strife and vainglory in their actions.

questions.question: What should each person do according to Philippians 2:3?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:3 encourages believers to esteem others as better than themselves.

questions.question: In Philippians 2:4, what are believers urged to consider?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:4 states that every man should look on the things of others.

questions.question: What mind are believers encouraged to have in Philippians 2:5?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:5 specifically instructs to let the mind that was in Christ Jesus be in us.

questions.question: What did Christ Jesus not consider according to Philippians 2:6?
options: Robbery to be equal with God
A shame to be a servant
A burden to take on flesh
A sin to die on the cross
questions.correctAnswer: Robbery to be equal with God
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:6 says that Christ, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God.

questions.question: What form did Christ take according to Philippians 2:7?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:7 states that Christ made himself of no reputation and took upon him the form of a servant.

questions.question: What was Christ's state when he was found according to Philippians 2:8?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:8 describes Christ as being found in fashion as a man.

questions.question: What did God do to Christ after his humility according to Philippians 2:9?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:9 states that God highly exalted Christ after his humility.

questions.question: What happens at the name of Jesus according to Philippians 2:10?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:10 specifically mentions that at the name of Jesus, every knee should bow.

questions.question: Is there any consolation in Christ mentioned in Philippians 2:1?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:1 begins with 'If there be therefore any consolation in Christ,' indicating there is.

questions.question: Does Philippians 2:3 encourage strife among believers?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:3 advises against strife by stating, 'Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory.'

questions.question: Philippians 2:5 states that believers should have the mind of Paul.
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:5 instructs believers to have the mind of Christ Jesus, not Paul.

questions.question: According to Philippians 2:8, Christ was obedient to the death of the cross.
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:8 clearly states that Christ became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

medium.title: Philippians Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Philippians Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should every tongue confess according to Philippians 2:11?
options: The Holy Spirit is our guide
questions.explanation: The verse states that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, emphasizing His lordship to the glory of God the Father. (Philippians 2:11)

questions.question: What does Philippians 2:12 promise will happen if someone works out their own salvation with fear and trembling?
questions.explanation: Working out one's own salvation is linked to obedience and reverence, which ultimately brings glory to God. (Philippians 2:12)

questions.question: Who works in believers to will and to do of His good pleasure according to Philippians 2:13?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:13 indicates that it is God who works in believers, influencing both their will and actions for His purposes.

questions.question: What should believers do according to Philippians 2:14?
options: Do all things without murmurings and disputings
questions.correctAnswer: Do all things without murmurings and disputings
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:14 commands believers to avoid complaining and arguing in their actions, promoting harmony among them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of shining as lights in the world according to Philippians 2:15?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:15 describes that believers shine as lights in the world so they can be blameless and harmless, reflecting God's character.

questions.question: What does Paul want to hold forth according to Philippians 2:16?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:16 indicates that Paul encourages holding forth the 'word of life' as a way to bring joy when Christ returns.

questions.question: What attitude does Paul express about his potential offering in Philippians 2:17?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:17 shows Paul's joy in the possibility of being offered as a sacrifice for the faith of the believers, highlighting his commitment.

questions.question: According to Philippians 2:18, how should the believers respond to Paul's joy?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:18 encourages the believers to share in Paul's joy, indicating the importance of unity in faith and experience.

questions.question: What is Paul’s intention regarding Timothy in Philippians 2:19?
options: To send him shortly to the believers
questions.correctAnswer: To send him shortly to the believers
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:19 reveals Paul's trust in the Lord to send Timothy to the believers, showing his care for their well-being.

questions.question: What does Paul express about Timothy's character in Philippians 2:20?
options: He naturally cares for the state of the believers
questions.correctAnswer: He naturally cares for the state of the believers
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:20 highlights Timothy's genuine concern for the believers, indicating his likemindedness and reliability.

questions.question: According to Philippians 2:1, what should exist among believers?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:1 encourages believers to experience consolation in Christ, which fosters unity and love among them.

questions.question: What does Philippians 2:3 advise against when interacting with others?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:3 instructs believers to avoid actions motivated by strife or pride, promoting humility and mutual respect.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul encourages believers to work out their own salvation with fear and trembling?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:12 encourages believers to work out their own salvation with appropriate reverence and seriousness, emphasizing personal responsibility.

questions.question: Is it true that God works in believers only when they are in church?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:13 states that God works in believers at all times, not limited to church settings, as He influences their will and actions.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul expresses concern for the state of the believers in Philippians 2:19?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:19 shows that Paul trusts in the Lord to send Timothy for the believers’ comfort, indicating a proactive approach rather than mere concern.

hard.title: Philippians Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Philippians Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Philippians 2:21, what do all seek?
options: The things which are Jesus Christ's
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:21 states, 'For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's,' indicating that all seek their own interests rather than those of Christ.

questions.question: How does Paul describe Timothy’s service to the gospel in Philippians 2:22?
options: As a son with the father
As a servant with a master
As a friend with a friend
As a prophet with a vision
questions.correctAnswer: As a son with the father
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:22 says, 'But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel,' indicating a familial and trusted relationship.

questions.question: What reason does Paul give in Philippians 2:27 for God’s mercy on Epaphroditus and himself?
options: So Paul would not have sorrow upon sorrow
So Paul could visit Philippi sooner
questions.correctAnswer: So Paul would not have sorrow upon sorrow
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:27 states, 'God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow,' explaining the mercy’s purpose.

questions.question: In Philippians 2:25, how does Paul describe Epaphroditus?
options: Brother, companion in labour, fellowsoldier, messenger, and ministerer to Paul's wants
A prophet, teacher, and preacher of the gospel
A servant, slave, and faithful steward
questions.correctAnswer: Brother, companion in labour, fellowsoldier, messenger, and ministerer to Paul's wants
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:25 describes Epaphroditus in these exact terms, emphasizing his multifaceted role and close relationship with Paul.

questions.question: What is the intended outcome Paul hopes for when the Philippians see Epaphroditus again (Philippians 2:28)?
options: They may rejoice and Paul may be less sorrowful
They may prepare a feast for him
questions.correctAnswer: They may rejoice and Paul may be less sorrowful
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:28 says, '...that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful,' which explains Paul’s pastoral care.

questions.question: Why was Epaphroditus 'nigh unto death' according to Philippians 2:30?
options: Because for the work of Christ he was nigh unto death, not regarding his life
Because he was persecuted by enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Because for the work of Christ he was nigh unto death, not regarding his life
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:30 explains that Epaphroditus risked his life for Christ’s work, showing his faithful service.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'kenosis' (κένωσις) in Philippians 2:7 mean?
options: Self-emptying or making oneself of no reputation
questions.correctAnswer: Self-emptying or making oneself of no reputation
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:7 uses the concept of 'kenosis' to describe Christ making himself of no reputation, a key theological term for his humility and incarnation.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Philippians 2:6-11 to emphasize Christ’s humility and exaltation?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:6-11 is a well-known chiasm, where ideas are mirrored to highlight Christ’s descent and ascent, a classic example of this literary device.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Philippians 2:10-11's theme that every knee shall bow and tongue confess Jesus Christ as Lord?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:10-11 echoes Isaiah 45:23, where God declares that every knee shall bow before Him, showing fulfillment in Christ’s lordship.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with Philippians 2:12’s exhortation to 'work out your own salvation with fear and trembling'?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:28-29 similarly exhorts believers to serve God with reverence and godly fear, corresponding with Philippians 2:12.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Philippians 2:21, which states 'For all seek their own...'?
options: A call to unity and humility
An exhortation to obey in Paul’s absence
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:20 precedes verse 21 and praises Timothy as 'no man likeminded' who cares for the Philippians’ state, setting the contrast for verse 21.

questions.question: The description of Epaphroditus as 'companion in labour' and 'fellow soldier' in Philippians 2:25 is an example of which biblical literary technique?
questions.explanation: Paul uses metaphor in Philippians 2:25, calling Epaphroditus a 'fellow soldier' to illustrate spiritual partnership and struggle.

questions.question: How does Philippians 2:8 use typology to foreshadow Christ’s death?
options: By describing Christ’s obedience unto death of the cross as the ultimate sacrifice
By linking Christ’s death to Old Testament sacrificial laws
By comparing Christ’s death to Moses’ intercession
questions.correctAnswer: By describing Christ’s obedience unto death of the cross as the ultimate sacrifice
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:8 typologically foreshadows the sacrificial nature of Christ’s death, fulfilling OT sacrificial themes as ultimate obedience.

questions.question: Does Philippians 2:24 express Paul’s trust that he will come to the Philippians shortly?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:24 states, 'But I trust in the Lord that I also myself shall come shortly,' confirming Paul’s expectation to visit soon.

questions.question: Is it true that Philippians 2:29 commands the Philippians to reject Epaphroditus upon his return?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:29 instructs to 'Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness; and hold such in reputation,' which is the opposite of rejection.

theological.title: Philippians Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Philippians Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Philippians 2:6 teach about the nature of Christ in relation to God?
options: Christ is equal with God and did not regard equality as something to cling to
Christ was created by God and is subordinate to Him
Christ is a mere man who later became divine
Christ only appeared to be divine but was not truly God
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is equal with God and did not regard equality as something to cling to
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:6 states that Christ, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God, affirming His true deity and equality with the Father.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in Philippians 2:12?
options: Believers must actively work out their own salvation with fear and trembling
Salvation is entirely passive and requires no effort
Sanctification happens only when the apostle is present
Salvation is earned by good works alone
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must actively work out their own salvation with fear and trembling
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:12 instructs believers to work out their own salvation with fear and trembling, emphasizing active participation in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the Spirit's role in believers is conveyed in Philippians 2:1?
options: The Spirit provides consolation, comfort, and fellowship among believers
The Spirit is only a symbol and not active in believers
The Spirit works only through miracles and not daily life
Believers should not rely on the Spirit for unity
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit provides consolation, comfort, and fellowship among believers
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:1 references the consolation in Christ, comfort of love, and fellowship of the Spirit, highlighting the Spirit's role in uniting and encouraging believers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Philippians 2:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:9 shows God's sovereignty as He highly exalted Christ and gave Him a name above every name, demonstrating divine authority over all.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is revealed in Philippians 2:13 as God working in believers?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:13 shows God's omnipotence as He works in believers both to will and to do His good pleasure, demonstrating His powerful enabling grace.

questions.question: How does Philippians 2:5-8 connect to the theme of the Incarnation and Atonement in the broader biblical narrative?
options: It illustrates Christ's voluntary humility and obedience culminating in the atoning death on the cross
It denies Christ's divinity and focuses on his humanity only
It teaches that Christ's death was accidental and unrelated to salvation
It emphasizes Christ's role as a political leader rather than a savior
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates Christ's voluntary humility and obedience culminating in the atoning death on the cross
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:5-8 describes Christ's incarnation and humility, connecting to the central biblical theme of the God-man who atones for sin by His death.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Philippians 2:10-11 establish regarding Jesus’ exaltation?
options: It fulfills Old Testament prophecy of universal recognition of the Messiah’s lordship
It contradicts the Old Testament teaching of God’s exclusivity
It suggests Jesus will be worshiped only by a small group of believers
It denies Jesus’ divine status by limiting worship
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Old Testament prophecy of universal recognition of the Messiah’s lordship
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:10-11 proclaims that every knee shall bow and every tongue confess Jesus Christ as Lord, fulfilling prophecies like Isaiah 45:23 about universal submission to God’s chosen.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Philippians 2:3 and 2:4 teach about Christian humility and love?
options: Believers must esteem others better than themselves and look to the interests of others, not just their own
Believers should prioritize their own needs over others
Humility means ignoring others' welfare to focus on personal holiness
Love is only a feeling and not demonstrated by actions
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must esteem others better than themselves and look to the interests of others, not just their own
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:3 teaches esteem for others above self, and 2:4 commands looking out for others’ interests, together emphasizing the active expression of humility and love.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Philippians 2:14 and 2:15 teach concerning Christian conduct and witness?
options: Believers must do all things without complaining to be blameless and shine as lights in a perverse generation
Complaining is acceptable when believers are persecuted
Good conduct is irrelevant to Christian witness
Believers should isolate themselves from the world
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must do all things without complaining to be blameless and shine as lights in a perverse generation
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:14-15 links obedience without murmurings to being blameless and shining as lights, highlighting how conduct impacts Christian witness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about gospel partnership do Philippians 2:22 and 2:25 teach?
options: True gospel partnership involves familial affection, service, and mutual support among workers for Christ
Gospel workers should act independently without mutual care
Partnership in the gospel is based on social status
Fellowship in the gospel is optional and not necessary
questions.correctAnswer: True gospel partnership involves familial affection, service, and mutual support among workers for Christ
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:22 describes Timothy serving like a son with a father, and 2:25 calls Epaphroditus a brother and fellow soldier, teaching gospel partnership involves close relational care and service.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Philippians 2:6-8 teaches that Christ gave up His divinity during the incarnation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Christ, though in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to cling to but humbled himself without ceasing to be divine
Christ ceased to be divine and became only human during the incarnation
Christ was a created being who earned divinity by obedience
Christ’s divinity was a disguise and not real
questions.correctAnswer: Christ, though in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to cling to but humbled himself without ceasing to be divine
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:6-8 affirms Christ’s pre-existent divine status and voluntary humility in taking human form, not the loss of divinity, consistent with orthodox Christology.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian joy and fellowship is highlighted in Philippians 2:17-18?
options: Joy is shared mutually in faith, even amid sacrifice and suffering
Joy is only personal and not shared with others
questions.correctAnswer: Joy is shared mutually in faith, even amid sacrifice and suffering
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:17-18 shows Paul rejoicing in being sacrificed for their faith and encourages them to share in that joy, highlighting communal joy in gospel service.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s mercy is demonstrated in Philippians 2:27 regarding Epaphroditus’ sickness?
options: God’s mercy extended to Epaphroditus to spare Paul sorrow upon sorrow
God’s mercy is arbitrary and unrelated to circumstances
Sickness indicates God’s rejection of a believer
God’s mercy is unconditional regardless of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy extended to Epaphroditus to spare Paul sorrow upon sorrow
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:27 explains God’s mercy in healing Epaphroditus and sparing Paul additional sorrow, illustrating God’s compassionate care for His servants.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Christian mission and self-sacrifice do Philippians 2:30 and 2:25 teach?
options: Effective gospel ministry involves risking life and enduring hardship for the sake of others
Missionary work should avoid any personal cost
Self-preservation is the highest priority in ministry
Ministers should seek honor rather than sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Effective gospel ministry involves risking life and enduring hardship for the sake of others
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:25 and 2:30 describe Epaphroditus risking death for Christ’s work and to supply the church’s lack of service toward Paul, teaching costly gospel service.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Philippians 2:19-23 reinforce about gospel leadership and pastoral care in the early church?
options: Gospel leadership is marked by genuine concern and likeminded care for the spiritual well-being of the church
Leaders act primarily out of self-interest
Pastoral care is unnecessary if the congregation is mature
Church leaders should avoid personal involvement
questions.correctAnswer: Gospel leadership is marked by genuine concern and likeminded care for the spiritual well-being of the church
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:19-23 presents Timothy as a caring, likeminded servant who naturally cares for the church’s state, illustrating biblical pastoral leadership.
